cue: How do you describe fake grief?

es.example: Lloró en la despedida, pero todos sabíamos que eran lágrimas de cocodrilo.
es.exampleTranslation: He cried at the farewell, but we all knew they were crocodile tears.

it.example: Ha pianto alla festa d'addio, ma erano lacrime di coccodrillo e lo sapevano tutti.
it.exampleTranslation: He cried at the leaving party, but they were crocodile tears and everyone knew it.

bridge.note: The same medieval slander against the same animal, inherited by both languages from the same bestiaries, and the whole difference is how many consonants each language kept. Spanish wore the word down to cocodrilo — one c, one l. Italian doubled what Spanish thinned: coccodrillo, with cc and ll. Neither is a spelling mistake for the other; they are two settled outcomes of the same Greek word, and the doubling is the single most reliable difference between Italian and Spanish vocabulary generally.

interference.es_to_it: Double both: COCCODRILLO. Italian gemination is not decoration — it changes the length of the consonant when spoken, and a Spanish speaker who writes 'cocodrilo' has written a word Italian does not have. The same habit runs through the vocabulary: Spanish oficina against Italian ufficio, Spanish común against comune, Spanish atacar against attaccare.
interference.it_to_es: Spanish does not double: COCODRILO, one c and one l. Spanish has almost no geminate consonants at all, so the reflex to double will always be wrong going this direction — and note lacrime/lágrimas, where Spanish keeps a written accent Italian has no use for.
